title: Mini-cascade onboarding: eviction budget & regional utilization proforma
content:
Purpose:
Quick back-of-envelope planning sheet for a ‘mini-cascade’ style model onboarding (small family of model variants rolled in a short window). Goal is to size eviction budget, regional GPU headroom, and KV cache delta for three rollout scenarios so SRE/Capacity Ops can provision minimal reserved slots and recommend a live rollout cadence.

Executive summary (one-liner):
If we onboard 3 variants (quantized 4-bit, 8-bit medium, fp16 large) into the US-EAST and EU-WEST fleets over a 10-day window, we need ~12% extra KV cache capacity in US-EAST and ~8% in EU-WEST to keep eviction rates < 2% under optimistic warmup. GPU slot reserves of ~6-8 GPUs per region (p99 request spikes) reduce tail latency during parallel warmup.

Assumptions (callouts):
- Active QPS baseline: US-EAST 4200 qps, EU-WEST 1300 qps (current prod week avg).
- Average request length: 45 tokens generated, 22 tokens in prompt.
- KV entry size: ~9.5KB per conversation on average (sparse context workloads skew lower).
- Warmup behavior: user traffic distributes 60/30/10 across model variants in first 48h (heaviest variant = quantized 4-bit serving highest throughput).
- Target eviction threshold: keep cross-shard eviction under 2% ideally; operational cap 5% for emergency.
- Warmup TTL staging: seeded shadow warmup for 10% of traffic, progressive open to full traffic over 72 hours in staggered cadence.

Workload profiles modeled (3 scenarios):
1) Fast parallel: all variants accept traffic day 0; shadow warmups small; rapid growth to full share in 24h.
   - Risk: KV pressure spike, evictions, higher tail latency.
2) Staggered: seq rollout with 48h spacing per variant; seeded warmup + burst queueing for 10% grace.
   - Lower peak cache delta.
3) Conservative shadow: 7-day shadow, warm traffic cutover; minimal production exposure until after 7-day warmup.
   - Lowest risk; highest time-to-traffic.

Regional delta math (back-of-envelope):
- US-EAST: expected new active convs = baseline active convs * 0.18 (estimated increase from models) = 1.8M -> delta convs ~324k. KV delta = 324k * 9.5KB = ~3.08GB (wait, math must be per-shard: actually 324k*9.5KB = 3,078,000 KB -> ~3,004 MB -> ~2.9 GB) [check units]. Add buffer for fragmentation/replication 1.35x -> ~3.9GB.
- EU-WEST: delta convs ~110k -> KV delta ~1.05GB -> with buffer ~1.4GB.

Eviction budgeting and safety margins:
- Eviction budget defined as additional ephemeral memory reserved across KV shards to absorb warmup high-water mark. For US-EAST set ephemeral reserve = 6GB (approx 1.5x delta) to keep eviction <2% under Fast-parallel.
- For Staggered set reserve = 3GB; for Conservative = 1.2GB.
- Translate reserve to GPU-slot safety by assuming KV+GPU co-hosting overhead 450MB per GPU; so 6GB -> ~13 slots of co-host overhead capacity (we round to reserve 8 GPUs for safety after considering pre-warmed caches).

GPU Fleet headroom sizing (rough):
- Expected token throughput increase: US-EAST +12% tokens, EU-WEST +7% tokens.
- Baseline GPU pool available for general-purpose: US-EAST 180 GPUs, EU-WEST 60 GPUs.
- If we keep p95 latency SLA, need to reserve: US-EAST 12 GPUs (6.7%) for rollout buffer; EU-WEST 5 GPUs (8.3%). These are soft reserves consumed by auto-scale policies.

Shadowing and warmup strategy recommendations:
- Use seeded shadowing at 10% traffic for first 48h, then 25% for next 48h, then full switch if KPIs look good.
- Pre-warm KV by replaying top 20k convs into local preload jobs per region (script: infra/preload/top20k-replay.sh).
- Apply per-shard TTL staggering: newer shards get shorter TTL to avoid immediate large memory soak; ramp to normal TTL over 7 days.

Operational playbook (quick):
- Pre-roll step (T-72h): create rollout plan in Console, allocate ephemeral KV-reserve (cluster tag: evict-budget-mini-cascade), schedule preload job to run in low-traffic hours.
- T-24h: enable seeded shadow 10% on canary fleet; watch evictions, p95 tokens, GPU slot saturation.
- T+0-48h: if evictions > 2% or GPU utilization > 85% for > 15m, trigger auto-throttle: reduce new model traffic by 40% and increase cache TTL for seeded traffic.

Monitoring & alerting knobs to add before rollout:
- Alert: cross-shard eviction rate > 1.5% sustained 10m -> pager to infra-runbooks.
- Dashboards: per-region KV footprint (daily), shard hotness histogram, model-variant ingress share, per-slot memory overhead.
- Linked logs: kv-evict-events-prod, gpu-slot-oom, warmup-preload-status.

Cost sketch (monthly incremental estimate):
- Extra KV memory reserved (US+EU) = ~9GB total -> cost delta approx $0.12/GB-month * 9GB = $1.08 (negligible; note our internal billing model charges for reserved slot overhead more).
- GPU slot soft reserve cost (12 GPUs US + 5 EU) * approximated reserved monthly rate $2,700/GPU-month -> ~17*2700 = $45,900/month. (This is a blunt approx to budget conversations.)

Open questions / to validate:
- Precise KV average entry size for these model variants (Lin to run sample dump).
- True replication factor per region (we assumed single replica local; if we enable cross-AZ replication cost changes).
- Will quantized variant change per-token compute cost materially and shift GPU headroom need? (Bench pending, PR #987).

Action items (owners):
- Daniel: run sample KV histogram for models (Jira INF-2345) -> due 2026-02-14.
- Lin: synthetic load test for fast-parallel scenario in us-east canary fleet -> due 2026-02-18.
- Marisol: prepare cost note for finance (monthly reserved GPU budget) -> due 2026-02-20.
- Ava: merge rollout doc into Console plan and request reserve via Infra-ops ticket -> due 2026-02-22.

Notes / rough scratch math included inline; treat as starting point. Prefer more conservative staggered rollout if any data gaps.

References and links:
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987
- Load test ticket: https://linear.app/REDWOOD/issue/INF-2345
- Console rollout doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Mini-Cascade-Onboard-Notes

Appendix (quick numeric table - textual):
Scenario | US-EAST KV delta | US reserve (GB) | GPU reserve (approx)
Fast-parallel | ~3.9GB | 6GB | 12 GPUs
Staggered | ~3.1GB | 3GB | 8 GPUs
Conservative | ~1.4GB | 1.2GB | 3 GPUs

End of sheet.
notes: Informal ops planning doc; stakeholder alignment required before converting to final runbook. Avoid simultaneous regional cutovers to reduce global cross-region pressure.
